kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-01.title: Skip the plants
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-01.body:
The carrot, the apple and the flower are not animals. The animals are the dog, the cat, the horse, the kangaroo and the baby kangaroo in its pouch: 5 animals.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-02.title: Match the edges
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-02.body:
Look at the curved edges around the empty place. The missing piece must have exactly these edges, so that it fills the hole without gaps or overlaps. Compare each piece with the hole, side by side.

Only piece B has edges that match the hole exactly.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-03.title: Count by animal
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-03.body:
The picture shows 3 hens, a cat and a dog. Hens have 2 legs: $3 \times 2 = 6$. The cat and the dog have 4 legs each: $4 + 4 = 8$. Altogether $6 + 8 = 14$ legs.

**Answer: (D) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-04.title: Count in one word
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-04.body:
K-A-N-G-A-R-O-O has the letter A twice. Written twice, that is $2 + 2 = 4$ times.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-05.title: Groups of four
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-05.body:
The stickers repeat in groups of 4: penguin, frog, bear, dinosaur. Stickers 1 to 4 and 5 to 8 are two full groups. Sticker 9 starts a new group (penguin), so sticker 10 is the frog.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-06.title: One letter per day
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-06.body:
BANANA has 6 letters. B on Friday, A on Saturday, N on Sunday, A on Monday, N on Tuesday and the last A on Wednesday.

**Answer: (C) Wednesday**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-07.title: Count the grid steps
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-07.body:
All the lines are drawn along the grid. Measure each line by counting how many sides of grid squares it runs along. Line E has the most steps, so it is the longest.

**Answer: (E) E**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-08.title: Upside down, same sides
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-08.body:
A reflection in water is upside down: the tree points downwards and the moon is below it. Left and right do not change: the moon stays to the right of the tree, and the crescent still opens the same way.

A and B have the crescent turned the other way, D has the moon on the wrong side, and E is not upside down. Only C is correct.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-10.title: Shared pegs
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-10.body:
Two towels next to each other share the peg between them. So he needs one peg at the start and then one more peg for each towel: for 3 towels $1 + 3 = 4$ pegs, as in the picture.

For 9 towels: $1 + 9 = 10$ pegs.

**Answer: (B) 10**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-11.title: Both get older
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-11.body:
In one year Betty is 1 year older and her sister is also 1 year older, so the sum grows by 2: $10 + 2 = 12$.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-12.title: Go back 3 hours
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-12.body:
The clock shows 2 o'clock. Three hours earlier: 1 o'clock, 12 o'clock, 11 o'clock. Lunch starts at 11.

**Answer: (D) 11**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-13.title: Step by step
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-13.body:
Each cut takes away 1 head and adds 3, so the dragon gains 2 heads.

First cut: $3 - 1 + 3 = 5$ heads. Second cut: $5 - 1 + 3 = 7$ heads.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-14.title: Count the squares
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-14.body:
Going around the board the pictures repeat in the order gift, clover, star, tree. So every group of 4 squares in a row along the path has exactly one star.

Count all the squares of the board: there are 36. That is $36 \div 4 = 9$ groups, so there were 9 stars.

**Answer: (A) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-15.title: Total and share
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-15.body:
Together they have $12 + 9 + 0 = 21$ candies. Shared among 3 girls: $21 \div 3 = 7$ each.

**Answer: (B) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-16.title: Read the row
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-16.body:
From left to right the paintings show: dragon, fruit (a peach), crane, flower, lion, tiger, butterfly.

The animals to the right of the fruit and to the left of both the lion and the tiger are in the crane and flower places. The flower is not an animal, so the answer is the crane.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-17.title: Half each
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-17.body:
They paid the same, so each paid $24 \div 2 = 12$ euros. Eeyore paid 12 euros for 6 cheese cakes: $12 \div 6 = 2$ euros each.

**Answer: (A) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-18.title: Jump by jump
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-18.body:
From START to FINISH there are 10 jumps (11 posts).

- 4 ahead, 1 back: after 5 seconds he is 3 posts ahead.
- 4 ahead, 1 back: after 10 seconds he is 6 posts ahead.
- 4 ahead: after 14 seconds he is 10 posts ahead, at FINISH.

He stops there, so it takes 14 seconds.

**Answer: (E) 14**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-19.title: Too many decorations
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-19.body:
She decorated $5 + 7 = 12$ times, but there are only 11 cookies. So at least $12 - 11 = 1$ cookie got both.

Exactly 1 is possible: raisins on cookies 1 to 5 and nuts on cookies 5 to 11.

**Answer: (A) 1**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-20.title: Per boy
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-20.body:
Each boy has $10 - 1 - 1 = 8$ candies left. Three boys: $3 \times 8 = 24$.

**Answer: (C) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-20.title: All together
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-20.body:
They had $3 \times 10 = 30$ candies. They ate 3 and gave away 3: $30 - 6 = 24$.

**Answer: (C) 24**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-23.title: Count every size
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-23.body:
1 big box, 3 smaller boxes, and $3 \times 3 = 9$ smallest boxes. Total $1 + 3 + 9 = 13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-24.title: Count rows and columns
kangaroo-ca-2012-g0102-24.body:
The board has 4 rows and 4 columns, so at the end there must be $4 \times 2 = 8$ coins. There are 10 coins, so at least 2 must be removed.

The third and fourth rows have 3 coins each. The first and third columns have 3 coins each. Removing the coin in row 3, column 1 and the coin in row 4, column 3 leaves exactly 2 coins in every row and every column.

**Answer: (C) 2**
